title: Steady toss height
whyItMatters: When the toss peaks at a different height each time, your swing has to re-time itself on every serve. Experienced servers keep toss height steadier than any other part of the toss.

detection.rule: Per stratum with n >= 10 usable serves: s = SD of toss apex height (cm) (1.4826 x MAD when n < 15); sigma = sqrt(max(0, s^2 - e^2)) with e from METRICS.md, else measurementErrorDefault; confidence = F_chi2(n-1)((n-1) x sigma^2 / T^2) x meanConf where T = fire threshold for the level. Eligible when confidence >= 0.70 and sigma / T >= 1.1.
detection.resolvedWhen: sigma <= resolved threshold for the level in a matched session, or a 'Clear improvement' verdict against the experiment baseline.

cues.outcome: Peak it at the same fence line.

drill.name: Fence-line toss ladder
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket. Pick a fixed line in the background, such as a fence rail, windbreak seam or band on a light pole, about a racquet's length above your full reach. Put a towel or racquet cover about half a metre inside the baseline, slightly to your hitting side.
steps: Toss 5 balls without swinging and watch where each one peaks against your line.
Serve 20 balls at a comfortable pace, swinging at every toss, even the imperfect ones.
Keep a count of the tosses that peaked on your line, within about a ball's height.
Finish with 10 serves alternating T and wide, without counting.
drill.successCriterion: 14 of 20 tosses peak on your line.
drill.progression: Call 'T' or 'wide' out loud as the ball rises and serve there, keeping the same peak.
drill.regression: Start with the racquet already up behind you and serve from the service line, tossing a little lower.

title: Same toss spot
whyItMatters: A toss that lands in a different spot each time drags your contact point around with it. Skilled servers vary this a little on purpose, so we only flag it when the spread is large.

detection.rule: Per stratum with n >= 10 usable serves: s = SD of toss-forward (cm) (1.4826 x MAD when n < 15); sigma = sqrt(max(0, s^2 - e^2)) with e from METRICS.md, else measurementErrorDefault; confidence = F_chi2(n-1)((n-1) x sigma^2 / T^2) x meanConf where T = fire threshold for the level. Eligible when confidence >= 0.70 and sigma / T >= 1.1. Never pool intended types: targets and serve types legitimately move the toss.
detection.resolvedWhen: sigma <= resolved threshold for the level in a matched session, or a 'Clear improvement' verdict.

cues.outcome: Every toss drops on the towel.

drill.name: Towel-drop check
drill.setup: Put a towel about half a metre inside the baseline, slightly to your hitting side, where your ideal toss would land if you let it drop.
steps: Before each set, toss once without swinging and note where the ball lands against the towel.
Serve 4 sets of 5 at a comfortable pace, swinging at every toss.
If a check toss misses the towel, change where you let go of the ball, not your swing.
Finish with 10 serves alternating deuce and ad courts.
drill.successCriterion: 3 of 4 check tosses land on the towel.
drill.progression: Swap the towel for a racquet cover and add a target in the service box.
drill.regression: Use two towels side by side as a bigger target and serve from the service line.

title: Toss in front
whyItMatters: A toss that drifts over or behind your head makes you arch back to reach it, and those serves often sail long or drop into the net. Coaches place the toss slightly in front so your body can move up and into the court.

thresholds.note: default resolved value = lower edge of the metrics.json toss-forward targetBand (20-60 cm, flat and slice first serves)

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the upper bound of toss-forward is below the fire value for its intended type (kick uses the kick row; flat, slice and untagged use default). With k clear of n usable: confidence = P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf; eligible when >= 0.70. contact-forward is shown as corroborating evidence only.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session mean toss-forward >= the resolved value for the intended type in a matched session.

cues.outcome: Missed tosses land inside the court.

drill.name: One-step-in toss
drill.setup: Place a towel one small step inside the baseline, in line with your front foot.
steps: Toss 5 balls without swinging; each should land on or past the towel.
Serve 20 balls at a comfortable pace, letting your body follow the ball into the court.
After every 5 serves, let one toss drop to check it still lands on or past the towel.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 4 of 5 check tosses land on or past the towel.
drill.progression: Serve from the baseline to T and wide targets without changing where the toss would land.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line with your feet side by side and a slightly lower toss.

comfortNotes.back: Flat or slice serves only for this drill.

title: Toss within reach
whyItMatters: When the toss is well out in front, you end up reaching forward instead of up, and contact comes lower. Hitting from a tall position gives the ball more room over the net.

thresholds.corroboration: session mean contact-height-ratio < 1.40, or net share of misses >= 0.6 with >= 6 misses
thresholds.note: 0.40 x height is about 70 cm for a 1.75 m player; resolved 60 cm = upper edge of the metrics.json toss-forward targetBand

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the lower bound of toss-forward is above 0.40 x standing height. Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70 and the corroboration condition holds.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session mean toss-forward <= 60 cm in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Toss where you can high-five it.
cues.outcome: Unhit tosses land one step in.

drill.name: Tall-contact toss
drill.setup: Place a towel about a shoe-length inside the baseline, in line with your front foot.
steps: Toss 5 balls without swinging; they should land within a racquet-length of the towel.
Serve 20 balls at a comfortable pace, reaching up to the ball rather than out after it.
Hold your landing still for a count of one after every serve.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 4 of 5 check tosses land within a racquet-length of the towel, and you hold 15 of 20 landings without stumbling forward.
drill.progression: Keep the same toss and add your leg drive, landing about a step inside the court.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line at half pace with your feet side by side.

title: Toss to your reach
whyItMatters: A very high toss is falling fast by the time you hit it, so small timing errors turn into big misses. In studies, skilled servers let the ball drop only about 55 to 75 cm before contact.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the lower bound of toss-drop is above 100 cm. Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. rhythm-release-to-contact is context only. A small drop is never flagged on its own.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session median toss-drop <= 85 cm in a matched session.

drill.name: Reach-height tempo serves
drill.setup: Pick a background line, such as a fence rail or windbreak seam, about 30 cm above the top of your racquet at full reach.
steps: Toss 3 balls without swinging so they peak at that line.
Serve 20 balls counting out loud: '1' as you toss, '2' as the racquet drops behind you, '3' as you hit.
Swing on '3' without waiting for the ball to fall.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets, counting silently.
drill.successCriterion: 15 of 20 swings start on '3' with the toss peaking at your line.
drill.progression: Add your normal leg drive and aim at a target in each box.
drill.regression: Start with the racquet already up behind you and serve from the service line.

comfortNotes.knee: Keep both feet on the ground; no jump.

title: Spring from your legs
whyItMatters: Your legs are a big part of your serve's power, even as a beginner. When players' knees were braced nearly straight in a study, serve speed dropped by about 15 to 17 percent at every level.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when knee-bend-band is 'low' with band probability >= 0.7 (a band reported as 'unclear' never counts). Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. Never fires on 'typical' or 'high': deeper is not better. landing-distance and contact-height-ratio are context only.
detection.resolvedWhen: knee-bend-band is 'low' on <= 30% of usable serves in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Sit on a high stool, then spring.

drill.name: Sit-and-spring serves
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket. Serve at a comfortable, easy pace throughout.
steps: Do 5 shadow serves: as the racquet goes up, sit down a little as if onto a high stool, then spring up towards the ball.
Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort with the same sit-then-spring.
After every 5 serves, check that you landed on or inside the baseline.
Finish with 10 serves at normal effort to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 15 of 20 serves land you on or inside the baseline.
drill.progression: Back-leg serves: balance on your back leg through the toss and serve, 3 sets of 8 mixed with normal serves.
drill.regression: Shadow swings with a small, comfortable bend, then 10 serves from the service line.

comfortNotes.back: Keep the bend small and the effort easy.

title: Tilt to hit up
whyItMatters: Tilting so your hitting shoulder rises above your tossing shoulder sets up an upward swing. Without that tilt, the swing tends to travel across the ball, which costs height over the net and spin.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the trophy reading of trunk-tilt-band is 'low' with band probability >= 0.7 (a band reported as 'unclear' never counts). Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70.
detection.resolvedWhen: Trophy reading is 'low' on <= 30% of usable serves in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Front shoulder up, like a see-saw.
cues.outcome: Swing up at the ball, not across.

drill.name: Point-and-tilt serves
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket.
steps: Do 5 slow shadow serves: as you toss, let your tossing arm point up at the ball so your front shoulder rises above your back shoulder.
Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, keeping the tossing arm pointing up at the ball as you load.
Count the serves that clear the net by a racquet-length or more.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 14 of 20 serves clear the net by a racquet-length or more.
drill.progression: Add a target deep in the box and keep the tilt at full pace.
drill.regression: Shadow swings holding the ball up at full reach in your tossing hand, then 10 serves from the service line.

title: Lift, don't arch
whyItMatters: A deep backward arch is hard to repeat and asks your lower back to do work your legs could do. Coaches get the lift from the legs and a toss slightly into the court instead.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the trophy reading of trunk-tilt-band is 'high' with band probability >= 0.7 (a band reported as 'unclear' never counts). Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. toss-forward is corroborating evidence only.
detection.resolvedWhen: Trophy reading is 'high' on <= 30% of usable serves in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Be a spring, not a banana.
cues.outcome: Toss forward; let your legs lift.

drill.name: Stacked serves
drill.setup: Place a towel one small step inside the baseline, in line with your front foot. Use flat or slice serves only for this drill.
steps: Toss 5 balls without swinging so they would land on the towel, in front rather than over your head.
Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, getting your height by pushing up with your legs rather than bending back.
Count the serves that go in.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 4 of 5 check tosses land on the towel and 12 of 20 serves go in.
drill.progression: Bring back kick second serves, keeping the toss slightly in front and the lift coming from your legs.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line with your feet side by side and the toss clearly in front.

comfortNotes.back: Flat or slice serves only, at about 70% effort.

title: Same rhythm every serve
whyItMatters: When the time from toss to hit changes a lot, it is hard to meet the ball in the same place. Skilled servers keep this timing remarkably steady, even when their toss varies.

detection.rule: Per stratum with n >= 10 usable serves: s = SD of rhythm-release-to-contact (ms), at >= 60 fps (1.4826 x MAD when n < 15); sigma = sqrt(max(0, s^2 - e^2)) with e = 1.2 frame durations unless METRICS.md reports otherwise; confidence = F_chi2(n-1)((n-1) x sigma^2 / T^2) x meanConf where T = fire threshold for the level. Eligible when confidence >= 0.70 and sigma / T >= 1.1.
detection.resolvedWhen: sigma <= resolved threshold for the level in a matched session, or a 'Clear improvement' verdict.

drill.name: 1-2-3 rhythm serves
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket.
steps: Say '1' as you toss, '2' as the racquet drops behind you and '3' as you hit, out loud and evenly spaced.
Serve 20 balls this way at about 70% effort.
Notice any serve where you had to wait or rush between '2' and '3'.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets, counting silently.
drill.successCriterion: 16 of 20 serves hit on an even '3'.
drill.progression: Keep the same count at full pace, mixing first and second serves.
drill.regression: Count from the trophy position, '1' as you toss and '2' as you hit, from the service line.

title: Keep it flowing
whyItMatters: A long stop at the top lets the stretch in your muscles fade before you swing. Coaches prefer one smooth motion with only a brief pause.

thresholds.note: fire value = metrics.json trophy-pause coachingFlag; trophy-pause is experimental by default, so this item runs only with the experimental toggle on until the metric is validated

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the lower bound of trophy-pause is above 500 ms. Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. Needs trophy-pause at >= 60 fps; while that metric is experimental, the effective tier is experimental.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session median trophy-pause <= 350 ms in a matched session with the same fpsClass.

cues.analogy: Flow like a wave, no stopping.

drill.name: Toss-and-go serves
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket.
steps: Do 5 shadow serves with no stop at the top, letting the racquet keep moving like a wave.
Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, starting the upward swing as the ball reaches its peak.
After each serve, ask yourself whether anything stopped; count the ones that flowed.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 15 of 20 serves with no noticeable stop at the top.
drill.progression: Full pace with a target in each box, keeping the flow.
drill.regression: Start with the racquet already up behind you, toss, and swing as soon as the ball peaks, from the service line.

title: Hit at full reach
whyItMatters: Hitting the ball higher gives it a better line over the net and down into the box. In studies, better servers made contact higher relative to their height, and contact height tracked serve speed.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the upper bound of contact-height-ratio is below 1.38. Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. Personal rule: a drop of >= 0.04 from the player's baseline with P >= 0.9 raises a minor 'slipped' flag.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session median contact-height-ratio >= 1.40 in a matched session.

cues.analogy: High-five the ball at the top.
cues.outcome: Hit at the peak of your reach.

drill.name: Reach-and-tap
drill.setup: Stand at the service line with a basket. Pick a target area deep in the opposite service box.
steps: Toss and tap the ball gently into the box with your arm at full stretch, 10 times.
Move back to the baseline and serve 15 balls at about 70% effort, reaching as high as you did for the taps.
Finish with 10 serves alternating T and wide.
drill.successCriterion: 8 of 10 taps land in the box, then 8 of 15 baseline serves go in.
drill.progression: Add your leg drive so contact feels higher still, at full pace.
drill.regression: Stay at the service line for all the balls; any ball that lands in the box counts.

comfortNotes.shoulder: Taps only, at an easy pace; skip the full serves.

title: Contact in front
whyItMatters: Contact behind your head makes the swing go up and back rather than up and forward, which costs control. Coaches look for contact slightly in front on first serves, with kick serves a little further back.

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the upper bound of contact-forward is below the fire value for its intended type. Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. Runs even when toss-forward is unavailable (apex out of frame); when toss-in-front is also eligible, stage order picks the toss item.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session mean contact-forward >= the resolved value for the intended type in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Meet it in front of your cap.
cues.outcome: Contact over the baseline, not behind.

drill.name: Brim check
drill.setup: Wear a cap if you have one. Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket.
steps: Toss and reach up with the racquet without hitting; the ball should fall in front of your front foot.
Serve 20 balls at a comfortable pace, meeting the ball before it drops past the brim of your cap.
After every 5 serves, repeat one reach-and-drop check.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: All 4 checks drop in front of your front foot, and 12 of 20 serves go in.
drill.progression: Hit first serves to the T with the same contact point, then slice serves wide.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line, flat or gentle slice only.

title: Stay tall through the hit
whyItMatters: Folding forward at contact pulls the racquet down through the ball, so serves dip into the net. Staying tall through the hit keeps the swing moving up and out.

detection.rule: Requires the contact reading of trunk-tilt-band (upright / fold); disabled if METRICS.md does not provide it. Per serve: clear when the contact reading is 'fold' with band probability >= 0.7 (a band reported as 'unclear' never counts). Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70.
detection.resolvedWhen: Contact reading is 'fold' on <= 30% of usable serves in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Tall like a lighthouse through the hit.

drill.name: Behind-the-baseline serves
drill.setup: Stand one to two metres behind the baseline with a basket.
steps: Serve 20 balls from there at about 70% effort, staying tall through the hit so you have to hit up to reach the box.
Count how many land in.
Step up to the baseline and finish with 10 serves to alternating targets, keeping the same tall finish.
drill.successCriterion: 12 of 20 serves from behind the baseline land in the box.
drill.progression: Aim for the deep half of the box from behind the baseline.
drill.regression: From the service line, try to make the ball's first and second bounces as far apart as possible.

title: Land into the court
whyItMatters: Landing behind where your front foot started usually means your body is moving away from the serve. Coaches want you moving up and into the court as you hit, which helps you reach higher and stay balanced for the next shot.

thresholds.note: landing-distance is measured from where the front toe started (metrics.json), not from the baseline

detection.rule: Per serve: clear when the upper bound of landing-distance is below -10 cm (landing behind where the front toe started). Eligible when P(p > 0.5 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)) x meanConf >= 0.70. If landing-distance is experimental at runtime, the item runs only with the experimental toggle on and carries the experimental tier.
detection.resolvedWhen: Session mean landing-distance >= 0 cm in a matched session.

cues.analogy: Follow the ball through a doorway.

drill.name: Serve and freeze
drill.setup: Stand in your usual serving spot with a basket.
steps: Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, letting your body follow the ball so you land on or inside the baseline.
Hold each landing still for 2 seconds before stepping back.
Finish with 10 serves at normal pace to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 15 of 20 landings on or inside the baseline, held still for 2 seconds.
drill.progression: Add a small jump, foot-up or foot-back as you prefer, with a controlled landing about a step inside.
drill.regression: Feet side by side, no jump: step into the court with your back foot after each serve.

title: A second serve with margin
whyItMatters: A second serve's job is to go in, and spin is what lets you swing freely and still land it. Coaches build it from a sideways swing path and a higher arc over the net.

thresholds.note: 0.70 is just below the vendor-reported recreational match-play second-serve in-rate of about 71% (research 01 [S7], Vendor claim); practice conditions are easier than matches

detection.rule: Second serves only (player-entered serve number 2, from per-serve tags or a tally). With k in of n >= 10: P = P(p < 0.70 | Beta(k+1, n-k+1)); fires when P >= 0.8; confidence = P x tagCoverage, eligible when >= 0.70.
detection.resolvedWhen: Second-serve in-rate >= 0.80 over >= 20 second serves pooled from matched sessions.

cues.analogy: Paint a rainbow over the net.
cues.outcome: Arc it high, drop it in.

drill.name: Spin ladder
drill.setup: Stand at the service line with a basket.
steps: Do 10 slow shadow swings that brush up and across the ball rather than straight through it.
Serve 8 balls from the service line with a high arc and a visible curve or kick.
Move back to halfway, then to the baseline, only when 6 of 8 land in from your current spot.
Finish with 10 second serves from the baseline, alternating deuce and ad.
drill.successCriterion: 6 of 8 serves land in from the baseline with a visible curve or kick.
drill.progression: Aim your second serves at the backhand side of the box.
drill.regression: Stay at the service line or halfway, slice only; any ball that lands in the box counts.

comfortNotes.shoulder: Slice at about 70% effort, 20 serves at most.
comfortNotes.elbow: Slice at about 70% effort, 20 serves at most.

title: Clear the net
whyItMatters: Most of your misses are going into the net. In studies, serves that netted differed from good serves mainly in the angle the ball left the racquet, so aiming higher over the net is the simplest first change.

detection.rule: Per serve number (first and second evaluated separately), from player-entered miss types. With m >= 6 misses of which j are net: P = P(share > 0.5 | Beta(j+1, m-j+1)); fires when P >= 0.8; confidence = P x tagCoverage, eligible when >= 0.70. minUsableServes here counts misses.
detection.resolvedWhen: Net share of misses <= 0.40 over >= 10 misses pooled from matched sessions.

cues.analogy: Throw the racquet up at the ball.
cues.outcome: Clear the net by a racquet.

drill.name: Net-clearance window
drill.setup: From your serving spot, pick a mark on the far fence or background that sits about a racquet-length above the middle of the net.
steps: Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, sending each one over the net through that window.
Count how many clear the net by at least a racquet-length.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 14 of 20 serves clear the net with room to spare.
drill.progression: Serve from one metre behind the baseline through the same window.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line, aiming at the deep half of the box.

title: Bring long serves down
whyItMatters: Most of your misses are going long, so the ball has enough height but not enough drop. Coaches bring it down with a little more spin and contact slightly further in front.

detection.rule: Per serve number (first and second evaluated separately), from player-entered miss types. With m >= 6 misses of which j are long: P = P(share > 0.5 | Beta(j+1, m-j+1)); fires when P >= 0.8; confidence = P x tagCoverage, eligible when >= 0.70. minUsableServes here counts misses.
detection.resolvedWhen: Long share of misses <= 0.40 over >= 10 misses pooled from matched sessions.

cues.analogy: Spin it down like a wave.
cues.outcome: Aim a metre inside the line.

drill.name: Drop-into-the-box
drill.setup: Place a towel about a metre inside the service line in the box you are serving to.
steps: Serve 5 balls at half pace, feeling the ball curve or dip down towards the towel.
Serve 20 balls at about 70% effort, aiming to land short of the service line with a little slice or topspin.
Count the serves that land in and the ones that go long.
Finish with 10 serves to alternating targets.
drill.successCriterion: 14 of 20 serves land in, with no more than 3 long.
drill.progression: Move the towel to the T or the wide corner at the same depth.
drill.regression: Serve from the service line; any ball that lands in the box counts.

comfortNotes.back: Use slice rather than kick for the spin.

title: Keep building
whyItMatters: Nothing stands out as a clear problem this session, so the best move is to build on what's working. Mixing targets and sides keeps practice closer to match play.

detection.rule: Chosen when capture-quality is not 'poor', usable serves >= 6, and no other item is eligible, or every eligible item is excluded by the player's comfort settings. Never used to hide a detected fault.

cues.outcome: Hit three targets in a row.

drill.name: Target ladder
drill.setup: Put one towel at the T and one in the wide corner of the box you are serving to. Serve at a comfortable pace, with no jumping.
steps: From the deuce court, serve 5 to the T, then 5 wide.
Repeat from the ad court.
Finish with 10 serves mixing first and second serves, choosing a target before each one.
drill.successCriterion: 14 of 20 serves land in, with 4 landing within a racquet-length of a towel.
drill.progression: Call the target out loud as the ball rises.
drill.regression: Use the whole half of the box as the target.
